record.paper_title: Banach spaces and Ramsey Theory: some open problems
record.original_question: If X is a separable non-Hilbertian Banach space, does there exist a sequence (X_n) of subspaces of X that are pairwise non-isomorphic?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. (G. Godefroy [33]) Let X be a separable non-Hilbertian Banach space. Is it true that there exists a sequence (Xn) of subspaces of X which are pairwise non-isomorphic?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $X$ be a separable Banach space that is not isomorphic to a Hilbert space. Does there necessarily exist a sequence $(X_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of (closed infinite-dimensional) subspaces of $X$ such that $X_n$ and $X_m$ are not isomorphic as Banach spaces whenever $n\neq m$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question (often attributed to Godefroy) is part of the program asking whether every non-Hilbertian separable Banach space is "ergodic" (contains continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces). Substantial partial results exist (e.g., for asymptotically Hilbertian spaces, Orlicz sequence spaces, near-Hilbert spaces by Cuellar Carrera and others), but the general conjecture remains open as of recent work.

status_evidence.title: The ergodicity of Orlicz sequence spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Each non-Hilbertian Orlicz sequence space contains continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress; the general conjecture that every non-Hilbertian separable Banach space is ergodic remains open.

status_evidence.title: Non-ergodic Banach spaces are near Hilbert (Cuellar Carrera)
status_evidence.snippet: If a separable Banach space is not ergodic then it must be near Hilbert.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result toward Godefroy's problem; problem itself not fully resolved.
